Changelog

DOAS 1.1.0 (2026-11-05)

Minor Release: Bayesian Diagnostics & Posterior Predictive Checks with bayesplot

This release expands the Bayesian capabilities of DOAS by integrating seamlessly with the bayesplot ecosystem for graphical Posterior Predictive Checks (PPC) and MCMC diagnostics.

Posterior Predictive Simulation & Model Checking

  • posterior_predict() S3 Method:
    • Simulates S×MS \times M replicated datasets (yrepy_{\text{rep}}) from the posterior predictive distribution of a fitted doas Bayesian model (method = "Bayes").
    • Double-observer sectors simulate from the multinomial capture-recapture process conditional on posterior draws of latent abundance and detection probabilities; single-observer sectors simulate from a binomial detection process.
    • Attaches observed survey counts as attr(yrep, "y"), making the output immediately compatible with all bayesplot::ppc_* functions.
    • Supports target predictions for total unique counts (type = "count"), joint detections (type = "both"), and observer-specific tallies (type = "obs1", type = "obs2").
    • Automatically handles unsurveyed sectors with drop_unsurveyed = TRUE.
  • pp_check() S3 Method:
    • Implements a direct S3 method for bayesplot::pp_check() on doas objects.
    • Supported graphical checks include:
      • "dens_overlay": Density overlay comparing empirical counts against multiple yrepy_{\text{rep}} draws.
      • "stat": Empirical distribution of any test statistic (e.g. stat = "sd", stat = "max", stat = "mean") with the observed statistic marked.
      • "stat_2d": Bivariate scatterplot of two test statistics (e.g. stat = c("mean", "sd")).
      • "bars": Bar plot comparing observed vs. simulated count frequencies (ideal for inspecting zero-inflation and clumped distributions).
      • "intervals", "ribbon", "rootogram": Sector-level predictive intervals and rootograms.

MCMC Diagnostic Arrays

  • as.array() & as.matrix() S3 Methods:
    • Converts multi-chain MCMC draws into a 3D array of dimensions [iterations, chains, parameters] or a 2D matrix.
    • Extracts chain-specific draws for total population abundance (total_abundance), mean detection probability (p_hat), detection covariate coefficients (p_*), and abundance covariate coefficients (n_*).
    • Enables all bayesplot::mcmc_* diagnostics: mcmc_trace(), mcmc_intervals(), mcmc_areas(), and mcmc_dens_overlay().

Package Infrastructure & Testing

  • Added bayesplot and ggplot2 to Suggests: in DESCRIPTION.
  • Updated _pkgdown.yml reference index to include Bayesian diagnostic methods under a dedicated “Model Selection & Diagnostics” section.
  • Expanded the unit test suite to 164 passing tests covering all new S3 generics, argument checks, dependent/independent protocols, and error handling.
  • Verified clean R CMD check with zero errors, zero warnings, zero notes.

DOAS 1.0.0 (2026-11-04)

Major Release: The Complete DOAS Framework

This major release marks the culmination of 9 months of development since the initial package release in March 2026. DOAS is now a mature, fully-featured, and mathematically rigorous package for wildlife census design, combining Double Observer (DO) mark-recapture/removal counts with single-observer block surveys and environmental covariate modeling.

Core Architecture & API Refinements

  • Canonical Inference Paradigms (method):
    • method = "ML" (default): Maximum Likelihood / analytical closed-form Chapman (independent observers) or Zippin removal (dependent observers) base estimators with multivariate Delta-method variance propagation across sectors. Fully backward-compatible with method = "frequentist".
    • method = "Bayes": Multi-chain Collapsed Poisson-Gamma-Beta Gibbs Sampler (Data Augmentation MCMC) sampling the full joint posterior of latent undetected groups f0f_0 and observer detection probabilities. Fully backward-compatible with method = "bayesian".
  • Observer Protocols (obs_type):
    • "independent" (default): Two observers scan independently (Lincoln-Petersen / Chapman geometry).
    • "dependent": Primary observer points out detected groups and secondary observer records only missed groups (2-pass removal / Zippin geometry).
  • Flexible Sector Pooling (pooling):
    • "hybrid" (default): Uses sector-specific double-observer estimates for DO sectors and extrapolates single-observer Block sectors using the modeled detection probability.
    • "global": Extrapolates all surveyed sectors using the pooled/modeled detection probability.
  • Boundary-Safe Confidence & Credible Intervals (ci_method):
    • "lognormal" (default): Implements Chao (1987) log-normal bounds on the unobserved component f0=N̂−Nobsf_0 = \hat{N} - N_{\text{obs}}, strictly guaranteeing CIlower≥Nobs\text{CI}_{\text{lower}} \ge N_{\text{obs}}. For Bayesian models, evaluates exact 95% posterior credible intervals directly from MCMC draws.
    • "bootstrap": Stratified non-parametric sector resampling bootstrap.
  • Solitary Species & Individual Counts: Full native support for solitary species (carnivores, territorial birds, solitary ungulates) where group size ≡1\equiv 1 and detected_groups == total_count.

Decoupled Covariate Modeling & Prediction

  • Detection Covariate Modeling (p_formula): Models primary observer detection probability p̂i\hat{p}_i as a function of environmental or survey covariates (e.g. p_formula = ~ effort + ruggedness). Fits a quasi-binomial GLM (ML) or a coupled Metropolis-within-Gibbs logistic regression (Bayes).
  • Abundance Covariate Modeling (n_formula): Models sector-level abundance λi\lambda_i as a function of habitat covariates (e.g. n_formula = ~ elevation + forest). Fits a quasi-Poisson GLM (ML) or a Poisson log-linear regression (Bayes).
  • Area & Effort Offsets (offset()): Supports offset(log(area)) or offset(log(transect_length)) in n_formula to account for variable sector sizes or transect lengths, yielding density estimates per unit area or effort.
  • S3 Prediction Method (predict.doas): Predicts expected individual abundance (type = "abundance"), detection probability (type = "detection"), or group count (type = "groups") for surveyed sectors or new data (newdata).
  • Unsurveyed Sector Imputation: Automatically imputes abundance and standard errors for completely unsurveyed sectors (total_count = NA) using the fitted n_formula habitat response model, propagating both process variance and parameter covariance into the total population estimate.

Multi-Chain Bayesian Gibbs Sampler & Diagnostics

  • Conjugate Beta Updates: Employs exact conjugate Beta full conditionals for detection probabilities. For dependent observers, the full conditional p∣x1,x2,f0∼Beta(x1+x2+α,x2+2f0+β)p \mid x_1, x_2, f_0 \sim \text{Beta}(x_1 + x_2 + \alpha, x_2 + 2 f_0 + \beta) remains strictly defined on (0,1)(0, 1) even in sparse regimes where the secondary observer detects as many groups as the primary (x1≤x2x_1 \le x_2).
  • Convergence Diagnostics: Automatically computes Gelman-Rubin potential scale reduction factor (R̂\hat{R}) and Effective Sample Size (ESS) with lag-1 autocorrelation correction across all chains for total abundance, sector abundances, and detection probabilities.

Data Ingestion & Formatting (doas_data)

  • Multi-Format Ingestion: Ingests and standardizes raw field sheets from:
    • "sector": Wide sector-by-sector summary tables.
    • "group": One row per detected group (long format).
    • "sighting": One row per observer sighting record linked by group_id.
  • Group Size Reconciliation: Supports "max" (default), "mean", or "obs1" reconciliation rules for sighting records.
  • Validation & Integrity Checks: Verifies tally consistency (detected_groups == groups_both + groups_obs1 + groups_obs2) and prevents misclassification of DO sectors with 0 secondary detections.

Model Selection (QAIC & WAIC)

  • Quasi-Akaike Information Criterion (QAIC): Model selection for frequentist quasi-binomial detection GLMs and quasi-Poisson abundance GLMs, using a common variance inflation factor ĉ=max⁡(1,ĉglobal)\hat{c} = \max(1, \hat{c}_{\text{global}}) estimated from the most parameterized candidate model (Burnham & Anderson 2002).
  • Watanabe-Akaike Information Criterion (WAIC): Out-of-sample predictive accuracy evaluation for Bayesian MCMC models using log-sum-exp stabilized log pointwise predictive density and pWAICp_{\text{WAIC}} variance penalties (Gelman et al. 2014).

Simulation Engine & Power Analysis

  • Population Simulation (simulate_pop): Generates cluster-sampled animal populations with environmental covariates and Poisson-distributed group sizes.
  • Survey Simulation (simulate_survey): Simulates field observer detections with detection covariates, group-size scaling, and observer count error.
  • Power Analysis (doas_power): Evaluates Relative Bias, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and 95% CI Coverage across varying DO survey effort levels to optimize field sampling design.

Documentation & Infrastructure

  • Full pkgdown website with automated GitHub Actions continuous deployment.
  • Comprehensive tutorial vignette (vignettes/DOAS-tutorial.Rmd) demonstrating ungulate and solitary surveys, offsets, and power simulations.
  • Official package hex logo in SVG and PNG formats under man/figures/.
  • 133 passing testthat unit tests and clean R CMD check status (Status: OK).

DOAS 0.1.0 (2026-03-04)

Initial Release

  • Initial implementation of the Double Observer Adjusted Survey (DOAS) framework accompanying Panaccio et al. (2024).
  • Core Chapman and Zippin estimators for independent and dependent double observers.
  • Basic simulation functions for cluster-sampled populations and survey detections.
  • Bootstrap and log-normal confidence intervals.
